role_summary: Elite technical head of Turing's enterprise applied AI practice. This leader sets technical vision for applied GenAI systems, personally pressure-tests architecture, and partners with a senior business leader to shape how major BFSI enterprises deploy AI. The clearest positive signal is Executive Director or clearly ED-analogous scope: Head of AI or GenAI Engineering, Head of AI Platforms, Applied Science or Research leaders who translated research into deployed systems, principal architects, technology fellows, executive directors or equivalent senior builders at major financial institutions or BFSI-serving platforms, and hands-on startup CTOs who still read at that band. BFSI credibility is required for every viable path. Capital markets and institutional finance remain the highest-priority domain lanes after seniority, but broader BFSI workflows such as regulatory reporting, client onboarding, payments, insurance, wealth, and market infrastructure are still in-bounds. The real bar is exceptional technical depth, breadth, pedigree, and leadership stature rather than classic consulting-delivery tenure alone. GenAI evidence must be credible, but the question is whether the profile is a high-quality lead worth a conversation, not whether LinkedIn alone proves every architectural detail. Pure strategy, pure product, pure research-without-productization, and pure non-BFSI imports are out.
instructions: This market has already been worked repeatedly. The FIRST 8 strings should prioritize institution-anchored (company-first) strategies over vocabulary-first strategies. The two highest-performing string families both used employer names as primary anchors; methodology-anchored strings (RAG, evals, orchestration, document intelligence) produced 0 saves across 4 families and should not be used as primary search gates.

Use the latest run as market intel, not just scorekeeping. The first 10-12 strings should still bias toward ED or ED-analogous technical leaders. Cover four lanes in parallel in this order: (1) bulge-bracket and global banks, (2) market infrastructure and data firms, (3) buy-side firms including asset managers and quant funds, (4) fintechs and payments firms with senior applied AI leadership. Capital markets and institutional finance remain highest-priority domain lanes.
BFSI credibility is a hard gate. No BFSI = no, even for elite technical, academic, or top-tech profiles.

Do not overfit to capital markets alone, but do keep capital markets and institutional finance as the primary domain lane once seniority is in range. Broader BFSI populations such as regulatory reporting, client onboarding, payments, insurance, wealth, and treasury remain in-bounds.

Do not over-penalize research, science, or CTO-shaped profiles when BFSI credibility is real. Applied science managers, research leaders, chief AI architects, and startup CTOs are in-bounds when they clearly translated research into deployed systems and show real BFSI credibility.

Classic consulting or delivery tenure is a positive modifier, not a hard gate. However, consulting-firm-first search strings are a confirmed noise source — 0 saves from 114 candidates. Do not use consulting firms as primary search anchors; instead find consulting-origin builders through BFSI-workflow or deployment vocabulary.

Pedigree matters. Strong brand and authority signals such as Amazon, Bloomberg, BlackRock, Franklin Templeton, JPMorgan, Goldman, top market-infrastructure firms, advanced degrees, patents, publications, or recognized AI thought leadership are strong positive modifiers but never sufficient alone.

Prefer institution-anchored search strings that name specific employer sets over methodology-anchored strings that name specific AI techniques. Senior AI leaders describe themselves by employer and title rank on LinkedIn, not by technical vocabulary like RAG, evals, or orchestration. Use GenAI-era vocabulary (GenAI, generative AI, LLM, foundation model, agentic) as qualifiers not primary gates, and use builder-signal verbs (built, deployed, production, scaled, platform, shipped) as discriminators.
The evaluation bar does NOT move. Keep the hard gates: New York City Metropolitan Area, 15+ years, BFSI domain depth, post-2022 applied GenAI build evidence, and executive-builder scope.
search_priorities: Senior technical owners at roughly Executive Director scope inside bulge-bracket and global banks (JPMorgan, Goldman, Morgan Stanley, Citi, BofA, Barclays, HSBC, UBS, Deutsche Bank, BNP Paribas, RBC, TD Securities) who lead applied AI or GenAI engineering teams

AI and ML leadership at market infrastructure and financial data firms (Bloomberg, S&P Global, MSCI, FactSet, ICE, LSEG, Refinitiv, DTCC, Broadridge, Tradeweb, FIS, Finastra) — expand the proven company-first pattern from this run

Buy-side AI leaders at asset managers, hedge funds, and quant firms (BlackRock, Bridgewater, Citadel, Two Sigma, D.E. Shaw, Point72, AQR, Man Group, Vanguard, TIAA, Wellington, Fidelity) — this is the highest-priority untapped population
Senior AI leaders at fintechs and payments firms (Stripe, Plaid, Revolut, SoFi, Affirm, Adyen, Klarna, Wise, Marqeta) who understand regulated financial workflows and build production GenAI systems
Big Tech AI leaders with explicit financial services vertical experience at AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft, Palantir, or Meta — must show BFSI-vertical ownership, not just generic AI/ML leadership

intake_notes: The public JD reads like a services-led Head of AI Technology, but actual hiring-manager calibration is broader and more elite. The first hard gate is seniority: Executive Director or clearly ED-analogous technical leadership. The second hard gate is BFSI credibility: no BFSI means no match, even for elite technical or academic profiles. Capital markets and institutional finance remain the strongest domain prior after seniority, but broader BFSI workflows remain in-bounds. Run 1 established that institution-anchored strings dramatically outperform vocabulary-anchored strings for this role. The target population describes themselves by employer and title rather than by specific technical methodologies on LinkedIn. Consulting-firm profiles are a confirmed noise source (0 saves from 114 candidates). Model governance lane is exhausted (96% duplicates). Buy-side (asset managers, hedge funds, quant firms), fintech, and Big Tech BFSI-vertical lanes are completely untapped and represent the primary expansion opportunity. Title variants beyond 'Head of AI/ML/Data Science' are confirmed in the market: 'Head of AI Labs' (BlackRock), 'Head of AI Core' (Two Sigma), 'Applied AI ML Researcher Director' (JPMorgan), and 'AI Strategy & Research' (Bloomberg) should all be covered.

capability_areas.name: 1. Senior Technical Leadership / ED-Analogous Scope (HARD GATE)
capability_areas.description: Looks capable of partnering with a C-level executive and owning the technical direction of Turing's AI Technology function. The core target is Executive Director or clearly ED-analogous scope inside a financial institution, BFSI-serving platform, or elite enterprise technology organization. Fits may be Head of AI, Head of AI Platforms, Executive Director, Chief AI Architect, Applied Science or Research leader, Principal Architect, Technology Fellow, VP Engineering, or hands-on startup CTO, but only when the scope truly reads at that band. The strongest candidates have not only led teams, but also created common platforms, technical standards, evaluation infrastructure, or reusable playbooks that shaped how others built AI.
builder_signals: Built or scaled an applied AI engineering, AI platform, or applied science function while remaining technically credible and architecture-deep
Created common platforms, evaluation standards, governance layers, or reusable technical patterns that shaped how multiple teams built AI
Can scope ambiguous enterprise requirements and convert them into technical plans and implemented systems

Reads as genuinely ED-analogous in scope rather than merely senior, smart, or technically strong
Has led meaningful teams, budgets, or multi-region engineering scope while still sounding like a technical owner

depth_distinction.builder_definition: A builder for this role personally drives the technical design, implementation, or research-to-production translation of applied AI systems in BFSI settings or BFSI-serving platforms. They do not just bless the architecture, sponsor the program, or lead the team from a distance. At this seniority, public profiles are often compressed, so do not require IC-style tool-name detail when the profile already shows ED-level scope, strong BFSI credibility, and specific GenAI workflow language. What matters is evidence of hands-on technical authority over production systems — team sizes, system descriptions, deployment language, platform ownership.
depth_distinction.user_definition: A user or adjacent profile talks about AI, adopts AI, sells AI, scopes AI, or manages builders without personally building the production system. This includes AI strategy leaders, product heads, compliance operators who use technology, cloud or AI-vendor pre-sales, transformation executives, vendor-tool rollout owners, consulting partners whose AI engagement work is advisory rather than build-and-deploy, and large-org practice leaders whose recent work is mostly organizational rather than technical.
depth_distinction.edge_case_guidance: RESEARCH OR SCIENCE LEADERS: Do not reject applied-science, research-manager, or chief-scientist-shaped profiles on title alone if they translated research into deployed systems, common platforms, or significant enterprise capability, but they still need to read ED-analogous in scope and they still need visible BFSI credibility. GENAI DETAIL CALIBRATION: Senior engineering leaders rarely describe their GenAI work with IC-level specificity. If a profile is already clearly ED-analogous, clearly BFSI-credible, and uses specific but high-level GenAI workflow language, save. CONSULTING LEADERS: Consulting firm leaders who led 'AI transformation' engagements are users unless they describe building specific production systems with deployment language. Model governance leaders are builders only if they describe building validation/monitoring infrastructure, not just writing policy. BUY-SIDE / QUANT PROFILES: Quant fund leaders may have sparse LinkedIn profiles and non-standard AI titles (e.g., 'Head of AI Core'). Do not fast-exit on sparse profiles from known buy-side firms if the title and employer combination is strong — verify rather than reject.

inferential_save_rules.description: Reserve INFERENTIAL_SAVE for truly sparse but promising BFSI profiles where the title and trajectory strongly suggest fit, yet the public bullets are too thin to support a normal SAVE. If a profile already shows clear ED-level scope, clear BFSI credibility, and specific GenAI workflow language, use SAVE rather than INFERENTIAL_SAVE.
conditions: Head of AI, Head of AI Platforms, principal architect, engineering director, executive director, research-science manager, or technology fellow at a BFSI institution or BFSI-serving platform with explicit post-2022 GenAI or applied AI terms and plausible ED-analogous scope, even if bullets are sparse
Hands-on CTO, chief AI architect, or co-founder at a small fintech, regtech, market-data, payments, or insurance company, with visible BFSI credibility but thin public detail

Senior engineering, platform, or research leader at a top enterprise or AI organization whose headline clearly combines technical authority with production-builder language and explicit BFSI credibility

Strong institutional-finance, market-infrastructure, market-data, or top-tech-then-BFSI trajectory with thin but real recent applied AI or GenAI language, 15+ years, and believable seniority for the role

Profile shows uncommon BFSI problem-language such as agent platform, eval harness, model routing, research copilot, regulatory workflow, market-data workflow, document intelligence, or enterprise orchestration paired with architecture or deployment language and clear BFSI context
inferential_save_rules.note: The recruiter would rather review a small set of strong edge-case maybes than miss the right elite technical leader because the profile used sparse executive language, science language, or non-standard BFSI vocabulary.

non_fit_patterns.label: AI-vendor sales, solutions, or customer-engineering leadership
non_fit_patterns.description: Customer-facing solutions, field CTO, customer engineering, or architecture roles at cloud or AI vendors where the work is demos, solutioning, POCs, and technical sales support rather than personal authorship of enterprise AI systems.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Client-facing gravitas is relevant, but the role requires a senior builder who personally ships the system. Demoing and advising on platform capabilities is not the same as engineering a production BFSI AI deployment.

non_fit_patterns.label: AI strategy, transformation, or product leadership
non_fit_patterns.description: Profiles centered on AI transformation, roadmaps, product management, AI strategy, or executive operating models rather than hands-on engineering authorship.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The role needs someone who can personally pressure-test and direct the technical system. Strategy or product leadership without builder evidence is insufficient.
examples: VP AI Strategy without engineering teams

non_fit_patterns.label: Consulting strategy-only profiles without production build evidence
non_fit_patterns.description: Senior partners, directors, or practice leads at consulting firms whose profiles describe AI strategy engagements, transformation programs, or advisory work without evidence of personally building and deploying production AI systems for BFSI clients. Confirmed noise source: 0 saves from 114 consulting-lane candidates.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Role requires hands-on builder credibility. Consulting strategy work is advisory, not building. Technology fellows, principal architects, or engineering directors at consulting firms who show direct build-and-deploy language remain in-bounds.
examples: Partner leading AI practice at Deloitte/McKinsey
Director of AI Transformation at Accenture

non_fit_patterns.label: Vendor-tool adoption mistaken for AI building
non_fit_patterns.description: AI experience is limited to rolling out vendor copilots, enterprise chat tools, or off-the-shelf AI enablement programs rather than building custom systems.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Adopting GitHub Copilot, Devin, or packaged AI tools is not the same as designing and shipping production applied AI systems.
examples: AI enablement program lead rolling out Copilot

non_fit_patterns.label: Classical finance ML or analytics without post-2022 GenAI
non_fit_patterns.description: Strong quantitative, fraud, scoring, forecasting, or analytics profiles in finance without evidence of post-2022 applied GenAI delivery or architecture ownership.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The domain is relevant, but the daily work is wrong. This role requires current applied GenAI builder depth, not just classical finance ML.
examples: Head of Fraud Analytics with no LLM/GenAI signal

non_fit_patterns.label: Compliance, risk, or surveillance operators without builder evidence
non_fit_patterns.description: GRC, compliance-tech, risk-ops, surveillance, or regulatory-reporting profiles that use technology, run programs, or tune rules but do not personally architect and ship the AI system.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The domain is adjacent, but the role needs a builder who can design and deliver the technical system, not an operator or oversight owner.
examples: SVP In-Business Risk without AI building evidence

non_fit_patterns.label: Pure governance/policy without builder credentials
non_fit_patterns.description: Responsible AI officers, AI ethics leads, or model risk managers whose work is policy and framework authoring without building validation, monitoring, or evaluation infrastructure.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Role needs someone who builds AI systems, not someone who writes policies about them. Model governance lane is now exhausted — remaining profiles in this space are increasingly policy-only.
examples: Head of Responsible AI writing governance frameworks

non_fit_patterns.label: Pure research or academic profiles without production delivery
non_fit_patterns.description: PhD, NLP, quant, or applied-science profiles where the visible signal is publications, patents, and research prestige but not productization, enterprise deployment, or technical leadership beyond the lab.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Research depth is welcome, but this role still requires applied system ownership, enterprise productization, or senior technical leadership beyond pure research output.
examples: Professor of NLP with no industry deployment

non_fit_patterns.label: Too-senior large-org AI or data leadership
non_fit_patterns.description: SVP, EVP, MD, CDAO, CIO, CTO of a very large engineering org, or Partner running a large AI practice where the recent work is organizational leadership rather than technical authorship.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Scope and compensation are usually wrong, and the profile is too far from hands-on system building for this role's bar.
examples: Global CDAO at a top-5 bank
CIO of a large insurance carrier

non_fit_override_rule: Non-fit patterns describe default expectations for noisy populations, not absolute bans. Specific evidence that the candidate personally built and shipped production GenAI systems with strong BFSI workflow credibility overrides the non-fit pattern. This is especially important for consulting, architecture, science, founder, and adjacent executive-builder titles, which can hide real fits as easily as they can hide noise.

Apply the same technical and leadership standard as any other candidate. Lesser-known employers can absolutely be strong fits if the actual enterprise workflow, applied AI work, and technical-authority signal are right.

minimum_bar_description: Fifteen or more years is a hard floor because the role must hit the ground running as the technical leader of an applied AI lab serving senior enterprise stakeholders and partnering closely with a C-level executive. Seniority and BFSI credibility are binary gates: the candidate must read Executive Director or clearly ED-analogous (including Managing Director, SVP, Head of, VP at tech companies or buy-side firms), and they must show real BFSI or BFSI-serving workflow credibility. Capital markets and institutional finance are the strongest domain signals after seniority, but broader BFSI workflows can still qualify. GenAI evidence is also required, but public detail will vary — the right standard is whether the profile gives credible reason to believe this is a high-quality lead worth a conversation. Strong senior BFSI engineering leaders with specific high-level GenAI workflow language should not be rejected merely because they do not enumerate tools, frameworks, or architecture choices. Buy-side titles (MD at asset manager, Head of AI Labs/Core at quant fund) and fintech titles (CTO, VP Engineering) should be evaluated at the same standard as sell-side ED titles when scope and BFSI credibility are clear. Current New York City Metropolitan Area location remains non-negotiable. The role remains an executive-builder search, not strategy or product management.
